events.title: Destruction of the Temple of Artemis at Ephesus
events.description: According to tradition, Herostratus set fire to the Temple of Artemis at Ephesus, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, reportedly on the night Alexander the Great was born. The date is traditionally given as July 21, 356 BCE, so the year here is approximate and should be read as 356 BCE.
events.significance: The loss of one of the Seven Wonders gave rise to the term 'Herostratic fame' for seeking notoriety through destructive acts.

events.title: First Battle of Bull Run (First Manassas)
events.description: Confederate forces under Generals P.G.T. Beauregard and Joseph E. Johnston defeated the Union Army commanded by Brigadier General Irvin McDowell near Manassas, Virginia. Confederate General Thomas Jackson earned the nickname 'Stonewall' during the fighting.
events.significance: The first major land battle of the American Civil War shattered Northern hopes of a quick victory and signaled that the war would be long and costly.

events.title: Birth of Ernest Hemingway
events.description: American novelist and short story writer Ernest Hemingway was born in Oak Park, Illinois. He wrote works including The Sun Also Rises, A Farewell to Arms, and The Old Man and the Sea.
events.significance: Hemingway's spare, economical prose style profoundly influenced 20th-century literature, and he won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1954.

events.title: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin Leave the Moon
events.description: After becoming the first humans to walk on the Moon, Apollo 11 astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin lifted off from the lunar surface in the Eagle module (July 21 UTC) and rejoined Michael Collins in lunar orbit. Armstrong had first stepped onto the surface in the early hours of July 21 UTC.
events.significance: Apollo 11 fulfilled President Kennedy's goal of landing a man on the Moon and returning him safely to Earth, a landmark achievement in human exploration.
